sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 4130 of 2022
Applicant :- Lakhan Yadav Alias Ram Lakhan S/O Late Parmeshvar

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
Counsel for Applicant :- Amit Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was married to the applicant.

It is alleged in the FIR that the marriage was a inter-caste marriage and subsequently,
allegations were leveled of demanding dowry.
It is also stated that the matrimonial family, including the applicant, had killed the victim and had burned the corpse.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant argues that it was a case of natural death.

He also relies upon the statement of the neighbours, who had stated that both the applicant and the deceased were Lakhan Yadav Alias Ram Lakhan S/O Late ... vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46301812/
1 living together and had no disputes.
The applicant is in custody since 21.02.2021 and has no criminal antecedent.
4. Learned AGA opposes the bail application by arguing that post-mortem was not conducted, as such, the applicant is also guilty of erasing the evidence.
He, thus, argues that the bail application should be rejected.

5. Considering the submissions made at the Bar, in the FIR, prima-facie allegations were leveled,
however, from the statement of the neighbours, which are on record, prima-facie, the prosecution story may not be established; the applicant is in custody since 21.01.2021 and has no criminal antecedent, as such, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Lakhan Yadav alias Ram Lakhan be released on bail in FIR No.443 of 2020,
under Section 498A, 304B, 201, 323, 504, 506 IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S.
Deva, District Barabanki on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
